alignments.note: Postpositive δέ rendered by the verse-opening Now.
Article governing θεός surfaces as the (rule 19).
The ASV gives peace no determiner, so the article has no the to anchor (rule 23); under rule 21 the case preposition of stays with the noun rather than leaving a bare of on the article.
Genitive noun rendered of + noun, headed on the noun (rule 17).

Second attributive article governing the expressed head noun θεός; the ASV renders the participle as a finite relative clause, so the relativizer is the participle's helper and this article realizes nothing (rules 23, 31).
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; who is a rule 7/31 helper and again realizes the ἀνα- of ἀνάγω. Headed on the lexical verb brought (rule 17).
Anarthrous substantival adjective; no article competes, so the supplied determiner is an ordinary helper on the nominal word (rules 51, 58).
Article preceding ποιμένα takes the English the (rule 19); the interposed attributive great does not displace it.
Adjective of the τὸν μέγαν attributive phrase, reordered before the noun in English (rule 15).
Article carrying its case preposition: of and the form one unit headed on the (rule 21).
Second attributive article of τὸν ποιμένα … τὸν μέγαν; the ASV writes only one the, which s010 takes, so this article has no English realization (rule 23).
The marginal note offers by for ἐν; the text's with is what is aligned.
Anarthrous αἵματι with a supplied the; no article competes, so the determiner is a rule 7/51 helper on the noun.

Both διαθήκης and its adjective are anarthrous, so the supplied determiner an belongs to the noun and rides discontinuously with it (rules 15, 58); the case preposition of stays with the noun and heads it (rule 17).
Attributive adjective takes a bare eternal, the determiner belonging to the noun (rule 58).

Supplied appositional even introducing an appositive carried by an articular noun phrase, not by an expressed preposition; rule 105 makes such an even its own added unit under rule 5, the article keeping nothing beyond what rule 20 already denies it here.
The genitive pronoun ἡμῶν occupies the determiner slot as our, so the article governing κύριον realizes nothing (rule 20).
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive our.
Name split from its title rather than sharing a head (rules 17, 26).

review_notes: All 23 source and 28 target ids partitioned exactly once.

Two attributive-article pairs decided by rule 31/23: s006 empty because θεός is expressed and the participle carries the relativizer; s014 empty because the ASV writes only one the for τὸν ποιμένα … τὸν μέγαν.

t025 even* is the one added unit; the competing reading folds it onto the article as a rule 7 helper, but rule 105 confines that fold to an expressed preposition carrier and makes an articular appositive's even added.
τῆς εἰρήνης follows rule 21's determinerless clause: article unrepresented, of on the noun.
αἰωνίου/διαθήκης supplied determiner placed on the noun per rule 58, not on the adjacent adjective.
